profile.reading: This facility is attributed in the registry to NTT, part of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, one of the largest telecommunications and IT services groups in the world, headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. NTT operates a global data center business, NTT Global Data Centers, under NTT DATA, Inc. The operators own about us page, fetched this session, states NTT DATA is a top 10 global IT services provider with about 30 billion dollars in annual revenue, operations across 33 countries, and about 3 billion dollars in annual research and development investment, headquartered at the Toyosu Center Building, 3-3-3 Toyosu, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-6033, Japan, though these figures describe the wider NTT DATA organization rather than the data center division specifically, and no data center division formation or acquisition date was found on the pages fetched this session. A previously confirmed, specific data center acquisition remains NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. This session reached the operators own services.global.ntt data center locations pages directly and successfully. An earlier sessions attempts to reach the ragingwire.com domain had failed and found no corresponding Wikipedia article, a negative finding this session did not need to repeat. reading.body:
VA4 publishes 32 MW of IT capacity. Across the 19 Virginia facilities on this site that have published a megawatt figure, the total is 1,326 MW, and VA4 accounts for roughly 2.4 percent of that sum, ranking 13th among those 19. Virginia has 326 mapped facilities in total, meaning the overwhelming majority publish no capacity figure at all, so the 1,326 MW represents a floor, not a ceiling, for the state.

Thirty-two megawatts of IT load is a meaningful but not outsized allocation by Ashburn standards. At 40 kW per rack, a common assumption for AI training density, 32 MW supports roughly 800 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more traditional colocation assumption, the same power supports roughly 3,200 racks. The operator has not published a rack-count or a per-rack power figure, so neither translation is the operator's claim, only an illustration of how the power budget maps to hardware depending on workload type.

The campus carries no certifications listed in the published specifications, so no certification-based qualification can be read from the data. The address places VA4 inside Ashburn's core data center corridor, which the state context confirms as one of the densest concentrations of published capacity in Virginia. Whether the site hosts AI workloads, who its tenants are, and what its power pricing or grid interconnection looks like are not published.
